entries.proposition: After pilocarpine status epilepticus, inhibitory GSK3 beta phosphorylation and beta-catenin rose slightly by day 3, peaked at day 5 and returned to control by day 7.
entries.snippet: there was a slight induction of pGSK3βS9 by day 3, reached a maximum by 5 days and then declined to control levels by 7 days post-SE
entries.anchor: Results / Wnt signaling is activated during the epileptogenic period

entries.proposition: The authors report that a porcupine inhibitor and a tankyrase inhibitor failed to affect basal or induced hippocampal Wnt signalling and attribute this to a likely lack of blood-brain barrier penetration.
entries.snippet: both LGK974 (a PORCN inhibitor) and XAV939 (a tankyrase inhibitor) failed to affect basal or induced hippocampal Wnt signaling. A likely reason is that these compounds did not penetrate the BBB.
entries.anchor: Results / Constitutive Wnt signaling in a genetic model

entries.proposition: Spontaneous seizures in HBP1 knockout mice were first observed by the animal facility and then confirmed by the authors, and HBP1 is described as a Wnt-pathway inhibitor.
entries.snippet: spontaneous seizures in HBP1-/- mice were initially observed by our animal facilities and subsequently confirmed ourselves
entries.anchor: Results / Constitutive Wnt signaling in a genetic model

entries.proposition: Basal beta-catenin and the pGSK-S9 marker are stated to be elevated in HBP1 heterozygotes and additionally so in knockouts.
entries.snippet: basal β-catenin and pGSKS9 were elevated in HBP1+/- mice, and additionally so in HBP1-/- mice relative to HBP1+/+ controls
entries.anchor: Results / Constitutive Wnt signaling in a genetic model

entries.proposition: With pilocarpine at 220 mg/kg no HBP1 knockout mouse survived more than an hour; at 150 mg/kg knockouts had no survival past one day and heterozygotes reduced survival.
entries.snippet: pilocarpine (220 mg/kg see Methods) and found that no HBP1-/- mice survived seizure induction for more than an hour. Titration of the pilocarpine dose down to 150 mg/kg still demonstrated significant sensitivity for HBP1-/- mice (no survival past 1 day) while HBP1+/- mice had reduced survival compared to HBP1+/+ mice
entries.anchor: Results / Constitutive Wnt signaling in a genetic model

entries.proposition: At 135 mg/kg pilocarpine knockouts had the highest number of severe (Racine 5) seizures with heterozygotes intermediate.
entries.snippet: Further titration of pilocarpine dosing to 135 mg/kg resulted in sufficient survival to observe a clear gene dosage effect for HBP1 genotypes, with HBP1-/- mice presenting with the highest number of severe seizures (Racine Scale 5) relative to HBP1+/+ mice, with HBP1+/- mice having an intermediate in severity (Fig 7K)
entries.anchor: Results / Constitutive Wnt signaling in a genetic model

entries.proposition: The survival panel legend gives n = 5 mice per group.
entries.snippet: Survival curves were made for the first 5 days after seizure induction. (n = 5 mice for each group).

entries.proposition: The seizure-count panel legend gives n = 11 to 17 mice per group.
entries.snippet: on the number and severity of seizures on a 5-point modified Racine scale [ 73 ]. (n = 11–17 mice for each group).

entries.proposition: 2-deoxyglucose was given at 250 mg/kg once daily from day 1 to day 5 after status epilepticus.
entries.snippet: Control and pilocarpine mice were treated with 2-deoxyglucose 250 mg/kg [74] once daily from day 1 to day 5 post-SE.
entries.anchor: Methods / Seizure induction and drug administration

entries.proposition: Mice were 7 weeks old and received 220 mg/kg pilocarpine (FVBN).
entries.snippet: 7-week old male FVBN (The Jackson laboratory) mice were injected intraperitoneally with 220 mg/kg pilocarpine (Sigma-Aldrich) in neutral saline.
entries.anchor: Methods / Seizure induction and drug administration

entries.proposition: The authors suggest a therapeutic window in early epileptogenesis and state that future work must test whether intervening in it attenuates chronic seizures.
entries.snippet: Clearly, future work will be required to determine if therapeutic intervention during the early epileptogenic window defined in this paper attenuates the onset of chronic seizures in epilepsies.
